name: libopenmpt
desc: Software library to decode tracked music files
why: Decodes decades of tracker module formats, a window into an unusual music culture, though it is a library first.

brief.what_it_is: libopenmpt is a cross-platform C++ and C library that decodes tracked music files (modules) into a raw PCM audio stream. It takes a module file as input and produces decoded audio samples for a host program to play or process. openmpt123 is a companion cross-platform command-line and terminal module player built on libopenmpt. The library is based on the player code of the OpenMPT project (Open ModPlug Tracker).
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as a way to decode tracker module music in cross-platform software, and says it avoids code base fragmentation by being developed in the same repository as OpenMPT.
brief.standout: It reuses the player code of the OpenMPT tracker rather than maintaining a separate decoder, and it ships a libmodplug-compatible layer (libopenmpt-modplug) so older software written against libmodplug can use it. It also has a plugin for the XMPlay player and a long tail of player and language-binding integrations listed on a wiki page.
brief.status: maintained. The homepage news lists releases on 2025-05-31, 2025-06-14, 2025-07-19, 2025-09-06, 2025-12-14, 2026-03-22, 2026-03-24, 2026-05-17, 2026-08-15 and a security update on 2026-08-19, with multiple release branches (0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5, 0.4) still receiving updates.
brief.caveats: The homepage describes the Winamp (in_openmpt) and foobar2000 (foo_openmpt) plugins as deprecated, in favour of WACUP or Winamp's own libopenmpt-based plugin and foo_openmpt54, a fork. The homepage does not describe install or build steps, and I did not reach a README or repository, so build details are unverified. The brew description and scout notes both frame it as a library first, with openmpt123 as the player.

judge.reason: It opens a door into tracker music: one library decodes decades of pattern-based module formats, and its companion player makes them easy to explore.

entry.title: libopenmpt
entry.tldr: A library and terminal player, openmpt123, that decodes tracker module music files, the compact song format of the demoscene and old PC games.
entry.deeper_look:
libopenmpt decodes tracked music files, usually called modules, into a raw PCM audio stream. A module is a song stored as note patterns plus the small samples that play them, rather than as recorded audio. The library takes a module file and hands decoded samples to a host program to play or process.

It is based on the player code of OpenMPT, the Open ModPlug Tracker. In the homepage's words: "In order to avoid code base fragmentation, libopenmpt is developed in the same source code repository as OpenMPT." The tracker and the library share one player, so a module should sound the same in both.

The Homebrew formula also installs openmpt123, which the homepage describes as "a cross-platform command-line or terminal based module file player." That is the quick way in: point it at a module file and listen. The deeper door is the format family itself. Tracker music is a distinct culture with decades of files, and a decoder like this is what keeps those files playable.

The library has a libmodplug-compatible layer, libopenmpt-modplug, so older software written against libmodplug can use it. A wiki page lists many players and language bindings built on top.
entry.install:
brew install libopenmpt
# installs the openmpt123 player; you need a module file (.mod, .xm, .it, .s3m) to play

try_this.what_happens: Lists the player's options and the audio output and file format choices it supports.

entry.whats_unique: It reuses the player code of the OpenMPT tracker instead of maintaining a separate decoder, so playback follows a living tracker. It also offers a libmodplug-compatible layer for older software.
entry.caveats: It is a library first, with openmpt123 as a companion player, and you must supply your own module files; the brief did not cover install or build details beyond the brew formula.
